reason: The arithmetic checks out and the perceptual claim it rests on does not. Driven at 1440 the small line spans x565.1-930.9 y1668.8-1685.8 and intersects exactly 6 of the 12 columns; the head spans x602.4-893.6 y1604.8-1630.8 and intersects exactly 1. So the counts are right. But the conclusion drawn from them is wrong against the pixels. Every column top sits between y1619.4 and y1657.8, all of them ABOVE the caption's top edge of y1668.8 - so the caption crosses no top edge, no dash, no silhouette; it lies entirely inside the flat fill body of the bars it spans. The head at y1604.8-1630.8 clears the skyline but for the single tallest column at y1619.4. That is not a collision, it is a composition: the head sits above the skyline, the caption sits in the dead fill below it. Rendered at 1440 and at 390 the twelve columns read unmistakably as a bar chart - shared baseline, uniform width and gap, rounded tops, a rising silhouette - with a caption set inside it, the ordinary watermark idiom. No text is obscured and no mark is destroyed. 'They do not read as a chart at all' and 'reads as a rendering error' are simply not what the frames show. Severity 'defect' - visibly wrong but passable - is therefore overstated; nothing is visibly wrong. Refinement at most. The proposed fix is also wrong twice over, and the second way is serious. First the numbers: the fix assumes 'full opacity' recovers a real chart, but --wash is rgba(17,17,17,0.03), so dropping opacity 0.5 takes the fill from ~1.5% to 3% ink (#fbfbfb to #f8f8f8) and the dashed top from 5% to 10%. It stays a whisper. To buy the reading the fix promises you would also have to darken the wash, which is a new stated-alpha tint and a fresh audit run. Second, and this is why it must not land: the twelve heights are invented - 38,52,44,61,47,58,50,66,54,62,57,70, a rising trend. Today the 0.5 opacity and the caption lying across the fill are exactly what mark that silhouette as a placeholder rather than a reading. Full opacity plus a real baseline rule plus 'its own faint value axis' - a scale for data that does not exist - converts a deliberately spectral placeholder into something that presents as a plotted upward trend over twelve periods, inside the one movement whose whole job is to refuse to draw that trend. That is the honest-degradation contract inverted: not a fabricated zero, a fabricated rise. The protected object is 'the trend the product cannot produce is drawn as the chart it would be' - would be, conditional, and the transparency is carrying that conditional. Removing it to gain legibility trades the idea for the rendering.
sharpenedFix: Keep the overlay, the 0.5 opacity and the two-line centred caption; the vertical placement is already correct (head above the skyline, caption inside the fill, crossing no top edge at 1440 or 390). The one true observation in the finding is that .ghost-plot has no baseline - the columns terminate in air. Add a single 1px dashed var(--line) rule along the bottom of .ghost-plot, inside the 0.5-opacity group so it stays as spectral as the marks it carries. That gives the bars something to stand on and costs no height, no new colour and no invented scale. Do NOT add a value axis: an axis on a plot with no data asserts a range the product has just said it cannot compute.
breaks: Were the stacked version built anyway: .ghost grows from 170px to roughly 240px (head 26 + small 17 + gap-hair 4 + gap-room 24 above the 120px plot and 48px padding), about 40% taller at the foot of the page, so the movement-three rhythm and the 390/768/1280/1440 scroll lengths need re-shooting; .ghost-say's absolute inset:0 and its 26ch head max-width both become dead code; the rise/--i:2 entrance now animates a two-row block rather than one card, so the motion budget in audit.mjs wants re-running; and any darkening of --wash to make the full-opacity columns read is a new stated-alpha tint that must clear the palette lock and the AA contrast check against the real composited backdrop. For the sharpened baseline rule, re-run audit.mjs only - it adds one hairline at an existing token and changes no box height.
